coverage: overnight since the evening brief (~19:50); X Following back to about 20:20
headline: The AI spending bill hits tech with the Nasdaq's worst day since June; Moderna sinks despite strong melanoma vaccine data; Trump says Musk restored Ukraine's Starlink, Kyiv says not fully.

stories.title: AI spending bill hits tech: Nasdaq has its worst day since June
facts: Nasdaq fell 2.6% to 26,008.86 and the S&P 500 1.21% to 7,663.43; the Dow ended flat at 52,867.98.
Chip stocks took the hardest hit: the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 6.7%, Lam Research about 12% and Nvidia about 4%.
Meta fell about 7% after its first quarterly cash outflow in over a decade, $135–145bn of planned capex and a plan for non-voting Class C shares.
SpaceX slid about 9% and Nebius about 7%; CoreWeave bond yields climbed to around 15%.
Investors fled to safety: the 10-year Treasury yield dropped below 5% in its sharpest one-day fall in over three years, while oil hit its highest since May on the Iran war.
Forbes counts $130bn lost by the world's six richest people in a day, about $74bn of it Elon Musk's.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the clearest sign yet that markets are starting to charge AI builders for the cost of the buildout rather than reward it.

stories.title: Moderna and Merck's cancer vaccine cuts melanoma recurrence by 42%, yet Moderna sinks
facts: Phase 3 INTerpath-001: intismeran plus Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone (HR 0.58) in resected stage IIB–IV melanoma.
Distant metastasis or death fell 38%; about 82% were alive without recurrence at two years, versus 70% on Keytruda alone.
After the six-month vaccine regimen the benefit grew to a 58% reduction; overall survival data aren't mature yet.
Partial data leaked before release; Moderna fell as much as 25% and closed about 17–18% lower, Merck about 1.8%. Analysts blame sky-high expectations after the stock nearly quadrupled since August.
Full results go to the ESMO Presidential Symposium this weekend and The New England Journal of Medicine.

stories.title: Trump says Musk "put it back" on Ukraine's Starlink; Kyiv says not fully
facts: The WSJ reports Trump called Musk on Wednesday to ask him to lift the throttling of Ukraine's Starlink and Starshield service.
Trump wouldn't confirm the call but said: "Bottom line, he put it back."
Zelensky said the military system's speed "has not been restored to 400 [km/h] yet"; a Ukrainian official said only some units saw improvement, and a European official told AP nothing had changed.
The administration and Rubio had denied asking for the restrictions, which came as Trump pressed Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries.
Finnish tech firms plan to help Ukraine build its own sovereign satellite system.

stories.title: Anthropic: Claude proves security properties at scale, auto mode goes default, GA on Google Cloud
facts: With Theorem, Claude formally proved security properties in the compiled RISC-V code of 123 open-source libraries, which Anthropic calls the first large-scale effort of its kind.
Along the way it found bugs that had survived years and trillions of test runs.
From next week, Claude web, desktop and mobile run in auto mode by default on Pro, Max and Team: an automated check blocks risky actions instead of step-by-step approvals.
You can switch back to manual approval anytime.
Claude models on Google Cloud (Anthropic-managed) are now generally available, with Google Cloud IAM, billing and commitment retirement.

image.alt: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale

stories.title: Quest Diagnostics breach, an iPhone spyware delivery network, and Vercel's push against static keys
facts: Quest Diagnostics told the SEC it found unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager on Oct 21 and believes some patient records were accessed; scope is still unclear.
Quest paused that system and several other clinician tools as a precaution; it says operations weren't materially disrupted.
Researchers told Forbes hundreds of websites with tens of millions of monthly visits are unknowingly serving as a delivery network for iPhone spyware.
Vercel surveyed 1,000+ SaaS vendors and found only 8.4% support secure machine auth; it's expanding OIDC, publishing an OIDC UI registry and setting auth requirements for Marketplace providers.

stories.title: Deadly Tibet quake, Taiwan shuts down for Typhoon Champi, Ebola trail leads to Entebbe
facts: A magnitude 7.0 quake hit Baqên County in Tibet's Nagqu region overnight: at least 16 dead, 65 injured, 339 homes collapsed and over 12,400 people relocated.
Taiwan cancelled all 262 domestic flights for Typhoon Champi; nationwide cancellations reached 977 flights, 596 of them at Taoyuan by 9am.
Africa CDC is checking whether the first Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe airport on 3 October; no link is established.
Kenya has nine confirmed infections and one death; Nigeria has its first case in over a decade.

image.alt: Powerful earthquake in Tibet's Nagqu area leaves 16 dead

stories.title: Quad9 will pull its free DNS out of France rather than block sports-piracy domains
facts: A French court ruled for beIN, ordering Quad9 to block DNS resolution of domains beIN says pirate its sports broadcasts.
The court cut the penalty from €580,000 to €1,000 a day, but Quad9 says it won't lie about DNS answers as a matter of principle.
The Swiss nonprofit will stop serving users in France from Tuesday, 24 November.

facts.text: OpenAI is reportedly raising up to $30bn at a $1.25tn pre-money valuation, led by Coatue and UAE investors; CNBC says Anthropic eyes $1.5–2tn for its IPO.
A Meta filing shows directors refused to let Zuckerberg keep absolute control if he sold stock; the compromise is non-voting Class C shares.
Amazon dropped its planned Loudoun County data centers after resident opposition and will donate 25 acres for an arts center.
Warhound, from Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, raised $200m at a $1.2bn valuation to genetically engineer working dogs for the military.
Raye won the Mercury Prize for This Music May Contain Hope.
Tom Skerritt, known for M*A*S*H, Alien and Steel Magnolias, has died at 93.
YouTube is moving Subscriptions out of the mobile bottom bar as it launches custom feeds.
Arc is sunsetting on 22 December 2026; new accounts are closed and The Browser Company points members to Dia, with a data export in the latest Arc.
A proof of concept for Node's Brotli bug (CVE-2026-111497) only reached code execution on a weakened build; no exploitation in the wild is reported.
Colin McDonnell teased Reylo, a relational loader that will hit 1.0 alongside TypeScript 7.1 stable.
Chrome's HTML-in-Canvas API lets you render live, accessible HTML inside 3D scenes.
Playwright PR stops Chromium making startup requests to Google.
